title: Wren and Mabel's Kite Rescue
markdown:
In a field that smelled like sweet honey and sunshine, right next to an orchard full of juicy apples, lived the happiest little robin. Her name was Wren. Her feathers were bright red, like a yummy strawberry. When she sang it sounded like lots of little bells. Ting-a-ling-ling. Tweet-tweet-twee. It made everyone want a happy little wiggle-dance.

Under that same sunny field, digging and snuggling in the soft earth, lived Mabel the mole. The softest cuddly brown fur, like a warm hug. Little paws perfect for wiggling, giggling, and digging tunnels faster than you can say dig-dig-dig. Her nose would wiggle, wiggle, wiggle whenever something exciting was about to happen. And exciting things happened to Mabel and Wren all the time.

One morning the sky was so blue it looked like a giant painted picture. The sun made everything sparkle. Wren was doing her absolute favorite thing: zooming and looping and flipping way up high. She loved seeing the world spread out below like a colorful blanket. Then she chirped.

“Oooooh. What’s that?” Her bright eyes spotted something wonderful and new. “Look, look, look. It’s a kite. A beautiful bright red kite.”

The kite was so cheerful it looked like a happy red splash against the big blue sky. As Wren fluttered closer, her happy chirps turned into a little worried tweet.

“But. Oh no. It looks stuck. Really, really stuck.”

Down below, by her cozy burrow, Mabel’s little nose started its special wiggle.

“Hmm. I wonder what that means. It must be something exciting.” She popped her head out a little further, blinking in the bright sun. “What is it, Wren?”

Wren zipped down faster than a blink and landed on a fluffy white dandelion that bobbed in the breeze.

“Mabel, Mabel, Mabel. There’s a kite. A gorgeous bright red kite stuck way, way, way up high in the tallest apple tree in the whole orchard. It looks like it needs a rescue, and I think we have to be the rescuers.”

Mabel’s tiny smart eyes looked up at the super tall apple tree.

“A rescue? For a kite? Oh, that sounds like a super-duper important job. And a job for us, too.”

Wren nodded. “It does. It really does. But how will we get it down? It’s so, so, so high.” She tilted her head. The kite looked as if it were tickling the clouds.

Wren, being the brave adventurous robin she was, fluttered up, up, up, until she was right at the tippy-top of the tallest apple tree. She hopped from branch to branch, little feet feeling the rough bark, peeking at the bright red kite.

“Oh dear, oh dear.” Her voice sounded small from so far up. “It’s really, really stuck, Mabel. The string is all twisted around a big poky twig. I tried to pull it, but the twig is too strong for my little beak.” She gave a little tug. The twig would not budge. “Twist, twist, twist.” A tiny bit bummed, but she knew she could not give up. Not when a kite needed saving.

Down on the ground Mabel’s nose wiggled with deep thinking. If Wren cannot reach it from up high, and I cannot fly…

She looked at the smooth thick trunk. “Moles are excellent diggers, not excellent tree-climbers.” She could not scamper up the bark like a squirrel. Then her tiny eyes sparkled.

“Aha. I have a brilliant idea.”

She scampered to the very base of the tree, right where Wren was watching, heart full of hope.

“Okay, Wren. You tell me exactly where the kite string is tangled. Point to it with your beak. Then I’m going to dig.”

With her super-duper speedy digging paws she started to work. Scratch, scrape, dig. She did not dig a big hole. She dug a special kind of ramp, a wiggle-worm tunnel that went up the side of the trunk. Not a big straight ramp. A series of little bumps and tunnels a mole could wiggle up.

“Weeee. This is fun.” She giggled, body wiggling with effort. A secret mole highway leading up the tree.

Wren, from a low branch, watched with wide amazed eyes, twittering directions.

“A little more to the left, Mabel. Yes, that’s it. Right there. The string is just above that big bumpy bit.”

Mabel wiggled and wriggled, following Wren’s chirps and the feeling of the bark under her paws. Strong little legs. Amazing paws. Inch by tiny inch. Her wiggly nose led the way, sniffing out the best path, until she was as high as she could possibly get, right underneath where the kite looked very sad and tangled.

“I’m here, Wren.” A little muffled, so close to the rough bark.

Wren flew down beside Mabel’s head, feathers brushing gently against soft fur.

“You’re doing so, so well. You’re amazing. Now the string is just there. Can you try to nudge it with your nose? It’s just the right spot.”

Mabel took another deep determined breath. She wiggled her nose, surprisingly strong, like a tiny furry lever. A gentle push. Another little nudge. She wiggled her whole head, little mole body trembling with effort. One final super-powered magnificent wiggle.

Pop. The string came loose.

The bright red kite, free at last, floated gently down through the sunny dappled air. It danced and twirled like a happy butterfly. Wren, with expert swooping, flew down to catch it carefully, and with a soft thump it landed right at Mabel’s little mole feet.

“We did it.” Wren hopped up and down. “We rescued the kite.”

Mabel beamed, nose twitching. She wiggled out of the last bit of her tunnel-ramp and stood proudly next to Wren. They both looked at the beautiful red kite, colors shining, then at each other. They did not say that a robin and a mole could do anything together. Wren only puffed her strawberry chest a little, and Mabel’s nose kept its happy rhythm, while the kite rested at their feet as if it had always meant to come down that way.
